result.summary: Re-reviewed lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex scoped to the new leading clause on validate/2 (lines 174-176) and the moduledoc's new 'Empty-declared_fields exemption' section (lines 112-125). The clause is a genuine pattern-matched function-head clause with a guard (`when declared_fields == %{}`), not an if/cond crutch buried inside the existing clause -- it sits before the pre-existing `def validate(%Graph{nodes: nodes, edges: edges}, declared_fields) when is_map(declared_fields)` clause and returns the same %{valid: true, violations: []} shape the general path would produce for a graph with zero violations, so callers see no shape divergence. Minor, non-blocking style note: `declared_fields == %{}` is valid in a guard but `map_size(declared_fields) == 0` is the more idiomatic Elixir spelling for 'empty map' -- functionally identical, not worth a rework cycle. No scope creep: the change is exactly the one short-circuit clause the design doc's Sec.2.5 calls for, no new abstraction, no unrelated refactor of the existing two-clause violation-walking logic. Moduledoc section is genuinely explicit, not vague: it states the exact trigger condition (declared_fields == %{}, i.e. VariableSchema.fetch_schemas/3 returned empty), the exact return value, the reasoning (schema registration is optional; treating zero-fields as all-references-invalid would block activation for every unregistered pre-existing definition), and confirms both call sites (Definitions.activate/2 and Definitions.validate_definition_graph/2) get the guard uniformly via the shared validate/2 entry point rather than per-caller special-casing. Independently re-ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` from a clean rebuild (248 files) -- 0 warnings, 0 errors.
